clue.text: Daily fare in legislature

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the food a person usually eats
second meaning: a parliamentary assembly, as in some European countries and Japan

explanation.surface: Someone eats their everyday meals in the parliament building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily fare' reads as canteen food served inside a legislature; 'in' simply joins two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a habitual pattern of eating and a formal national assembly, such as the Japanese or historical German parliaments.

clue.text: Island dimness — last to leave house

indicators.note: the final letter departs from the word before it, so that word is cut short at its end

parts.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island
gloom is darkness or dimness

explanation.surface: On a dim island, the last person leaves a house.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus GLOOM without its final M gives IGLOO.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped dwelling built from blocks of snow, traditionally by Inuit people, so it is a kind of home.

clue.text: Formal written work — pleasant surprise is estimation originally

parts.note: a treat is an unexpected delight
taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning, so only the opening letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of estimation

explanation.surface: An assessment of a scholarly book turns out to be a pleasant surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a lengthy, systematic essay or book dealing formally with a particular subject.

clue.text: Easy to manage party (Channel Islands) meeting the French

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, British islands off the French coast
le is French for 'the' (masculine)

explanation.surface: A party held in the Channel Islands, where locals meet French visitors, goes smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Docile describes a person or animal that is compliant, submissive and readily controlled or taught.

clue.text: In centre, gorgeous small sign

indicators.note: in centre tells us to keep only the letters sitting at the middle of the next word

parts.note: the two central letters of this eight-letter word
mini means small, as in a miniskirt or Mini car

explanation.surface: A small, gorgeous sign hangs in the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' here is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is the third of the twelve zodiac signs, covering birthdays from late May to late June.

clue.text: Ultimately back the game plan as shrewd

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so we take the final letter of each following word

parts.note: the closing letters of all four words

explanation.surface: A coach finally supports the team's tactics as clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen can mean sharp or acute in mind, as in a keen intellect, which matches being astute and perceptive.

clue.text: President, unexpected vote loser?

indicators.note: something unexpected does not come out as planned, so the letters land in a surprising new order

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A head of state unexpectedly loses the election.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that Franklin Roosevelt won four presidential elections, so he was anything but a vote loser.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt served as heads of state of the United States.

clue.text: To some extent bit odd, leggy — move unsteadily

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so the solution is part of the run of words that follows

parts.note: concealed across the end of bit, all of odd, and the start of leggy

explanation.surface: A gangly foal looks a bit odd and leggy as it wobbles about.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk with short, tottering steps, like a small child just learning.

clue.text: Escape from charge surrounding lake

indicators.note: surrounding means going round the outside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a fee is a payment charged
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone escapes an accusation concerning a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an accusation to escape from, but it is a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away or get away from danger, the same action as making an escape.

clue.text: Devoted fan of Aida icon possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could form something else when arranged another way

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Is a devoted admirer of the star of Verdi's opera Aida a true enthusiast?
explanation.walkthrough: The word is Spanish in origin, first used of bullfighting fans, and suits opera buffs well.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a person who is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about an activity or subject.

clue.text: Italian river, right? Left!

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
RT is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone giving directions by an Italian river says 'Right?' and is corrected: 'Left!'
explanation.walkthrough: The exchange of right and left looks like the whole joke; 'Left' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, port is the nautical term for the side on your left when facing the bow.

clue.text: False alibi — event sure to happen!

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so the letters are not to be trusted in their present order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suspect's made-up alibi for the incident was bound to be exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inevitable describes something certain to occur and impossible to avoid or prevent.

clue.text: Through Virginia, coming across inn at first

indicators.note: coming across is read as spanning or straddling, so one part lies over the other on both sides

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: at first means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the preceding word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of inn

explanation.surface: A traveller passes through Virginia and comes upon an inn first.
explanation.definitionFit: Via is a preposition meaning by way of, travelling by a route that passes a given place.

clue.text: Entertaining story from date once recollected

indicators.note: read as re-collected, gathered together again, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells an amusing tale remembered from a date long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembering; split it as re-collected.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short, amusing or interesting account of a real incident or person.

clue.text: Far away, referring to car test, English

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles over three years old
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A garage in a distant spot writes about an English vehicle inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means situated a long distance from towns or other people, distant and isolated.

clue.text: Container receipt missing one parcel we oddly overlooked

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the word before loses something named straight after

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I, here removed

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions are passed over, so only the even ones survive

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A delivery container had no receipt, and our parcel was somehow forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: RECEIPT without I gives RECEPT; keeping only the even letters of PARCELWE gives ACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is any object or space used to hold or contain something, such as a bin or bowl.

clue.text: Excitement of 60 minutes inside where money is kept

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other, which encloses it

parts.note: a till is a shop's cash drawer
HR is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Spending an hour in the bank vault gives someone a buzz.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden feeling of excitement and pleasure, a rush or buzz.

clue.text: Cowardly cold flier, croaking

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a raven is a bird with a deep croaking call

explanation.surface: A timid, chilly pilot is losing their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a pilot, but it is a bird; 'croaking' pins down which one.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means contemptibly lacking in courage, a literary synonym for spineless or fearful.

clue.text: Fellow, international player, embracing Henry

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so one word wraps its arms around the other

parts.note: a cap is a player picked for the national team, who traditionally receives a cap
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A teammate of an international footballer gives a hug to Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is an informal British word for a man or bloke, so it matches fellow.

clue.text: In the end, not finishing book

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the phrase before loses its final letter

parts.note: at last means eventually, finally

explanation.surface: A reader finally gives up without finishing a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound volume of maps, so it is one particular kind of book.

clue.text: Place of great beauty, old and new, exotic, welcoming King

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so one piece is let inside the other
exotic means strikingly foreign and unfamiliar, so the letters take on a strange new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A beautiful exotic resort, both old and new, welcomes a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonderland is a land or setting full of marvels, delightfully lovely or magical scenery.

clue.text: Sullen mood, ours? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only partly, so the solution is a portion of the words just before

parts.note: concealed across the last letter of mood and the start of ours

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the gloomy atmosphere is entirely their own fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour describes a person who is severe, stern and gloomy in manner or appearance.

clue.text: Unique, extremely open, lovely!

indicators.note: extremely is read as at the extremes, so each of the next two words gives its outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters of open
first and last letters of lovely

explanation.surface: Someone gushes about a one-of-a-kind, very welcoming and lovely place.
explanation.definitionFit: Only as an adjective means sole or single of its kind, as in an only child.

clue.text: Enthusiastic European person (strong) that is not heartless

indicators.note: heartless means without a heart, so the middle letter of the word before goes

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a bull of a man is a big, powerful person
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strong European, who is not cold-hearted, is full of enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT without its middle O gives NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullient means cheerful and full of energy, bubbling over with high spirits.

clue.text: Bridge player's big meal lacking starter

indicators.note: lacking starter means without its first course, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a feast is a large, lavish meal

explanation.surface: A card player's banquet comes without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' sits naturally with a meal as an appetiser, but here it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, and East partners West against North and South.
